resources.string: Hear about trouble before you leave
Add the lines you take most days, from where you get on to where you get off, and when you travel. If TfL reports a closure or delays on that stretch, you\'ll get a notification.
That\'s the most alerts a phone can have (%s). Delete one to add another.
That\'s the most lines one alert can have (%s).
That\'s the most times one alert can have (%s).
Couldn\'t reach the alerts server, so notifications may be out of date. It tries again when you come back to Polaris.
This phone\'s secure storage can\'t be read just now, so the alerts server wasn\'t told. It tries again when you come back to Polaris.
Alerts need a server to watch TfL while Polaris is closed, and this phone isn\'t set up with one. Enter its address and token in Settings, under Alerts server; the README says how to run your own.

Polaris checks TfL every two minutes during the times you set, and tells you once per disruption, again if it gets worse, and when it has ended. Closures and delays come as urgent notifications, which you can let through Do Not Disturb; minor delays and planned works are ordinary ones. Planned works for the next day come the evening before, at 7 pm.
Notifications aren\'t set up in this build
This build of Polaris has no push service, so no notification can arrive. Your alerts still show what TfL says whenever you open Polaris. The README says how to build with your own Firebase project.
This phone can\'t receive notifications from Polaris
Alerts arrive through Google Play services, which this phone doesn\'t have or has switched off. Your alerts still show what TfL says whenever you open Polaris.
This phone couldn\'t be set up to receive notifications just now, so none can arrive yet.
Registering this phone for notifications. None can arrive until that is done.
This phone\'s registration with the alerts server was lost with its secure storage, so it has been registered afresh. Your alerts are as they were.
Your alerts server can\'t send to Android phones yet, so no notification will arrive. Whoever runs it needs to finish its Android setup; the README says how.
Polaris can only tell you about trouble if it may send notifications.
Turn them on in the phone\'s settings to hear about trouble.
On. To hear them during Do Not Disturb, allow it in the phone\'s settings for this kind.
Turned off in the phone\'s settings: you won\'t hear about closures or delays.
Opens the phone\'s settings for these notifications
Sent. It should arrive in a few seconds.
This phone isn\'t registered with the alerts server yet. Try again in a moment.
A closure or delays on a line you\'ve asked to hear about, while you travel.
Minor delays, tomorrow\'s planned works, and when trouble you were told about has ended.
Follow-ups that change a notice you already have, without a sound.
This is a test of your alerts, sent because you asked for one.
Closures and delays anywhere between your stations count, and station closures where you get on or off.
A time can\'t start and end together.
Each time goes the way set under ‘Which way’ unless you give it its own.
Each time goes the way set under ‘Which way’ unless you give it its own. Trouble TfL reports one way only counts when it\'s towards %s.
Each time goes the way set under ‘Which way’ unless you give it its own. Trouble TfL reports one way only counts at times going that way.
Polaris checks during these times only. Planned works for the next day come the evening before.

Watches TfL while Polaris is closed and sends notifications for your lines. Each person runs their own.
